title: 2013 Cranbrook Legal Studies Trial
notes: No answer key is included in the PDF; all answers are reasoned estimates. The Juliette scenario is shared by questions 9 and 10. No figures occur in Section I.

groups.stimulus: Juliette is the personal assistant of an international company based in Melbourne. She is charged with embezzling $250 000 from the company.

questions.stem: Max hides Rodolfo in his holiday home after he is involved in an armed robbery. Max can be charged as?
questions.answerNote: Helping an offender after the offence makes Max an accessory after the fact.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a treaty that enshrines human rights?

options.B: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
options.C: The United States Bill of Rights

questions.answerNote: The Convention on the Rights of the Child is a human rights treaty.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes state sovereignty?

options.A: The right of a person to vote in a state government election
options.B: The right of a group of people to determine its own future
options.C: The right of a state to make laws for its citizens
options.D: The right of a person to vote in a federal government election

questions.answerNote: State sovereignty includes a state’s authority to make laws for its population.

questions.stem: Penelope was speeding on her new Honda 125cc motorbike and was stopped by a male police officer who decided not to issue a speeding ticket. What feature of the legal system does this scenario demonstrate?
questions.answerNote: The officer’s choice whether to issue a ticket is police discretion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of situational crime prevention?

options.A: Creating alcohol free zones to reduce alcohol related crime
options.B: Establishing social skill programs for “children at risk”
options.C: Raising the school leaving age in NSW to 17 years
options.D: Establishing parenting workshops in disadvantaged areas

questions.answerNote: Alcohol-free zones alter the immediate environment and opportunities for offending.

questions.stem: Which of the following human rights are regarded as a collective right?
questions.answerNote: Self-determination is exercised collectively by peoples.

questions.stem: Selling alcohol to people under the age of 18 is an example of what type of crime?
questions.answerNote: Selling alcohol to a minor is a strict liability offence.

questions.stem: Stuart, a 15 year old indigenous youth, is held in remand on drug possession charges. He is found dead in his cell the following morning. An inquest into Stuart’s death will be held in what court?
questions.answerNote: A coroner investigates deaths requiring an inquest.

questions.stem: The main factors affecting Juliette’s criminal behaviour are
questions.answerNote: The scenario describes embezzlement to benefit the offender, indicating self-interest.

questions.stem: Juliette’s committal hearing will be heard in what court?
questions.answerNote: Committal proceedings are heard in the Local Court.

questions.stem: Which group of defences below constitute complete defences in criminal charges?
questions.answerNote: Self-defence, duress and insanity can be complete defences; Provocation and diminished responsibility are partial defences.

questions.stem: Which one of the following crimes is heard by the International Criminal Court?
questions.answerNote: Genocide is one of the ICC’s core crimes.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a non-legal measure that addresses human rights issues?

options.B: Decisions by the International Court of Justice
options.D: Published reports in the Australian media

questions.answerNote: Media reporting is a non-legal response.

questions.stem: What is the main aim of diversionary programs?
questions.answerNote: Diversionary programs (cautions, conferences, Drug Court) aim mainly at rehabilitation (B); D 'Deterrent' is the other plausible choice but is secondary.

questions.stem: Extradition involves:

options.A: Charging a person with the same crime in two locations
options.B: A person being prosecuted in the International Criminal Court
options.C: Charging a person with a transnational crime
options.D: Returning a person to the jurisdiction in which they committed the crime

questions.answerNote: Extradition returns a suspect or offender to the jurisdiction seeking them.

questions.stem: At her sentencing hearing, Helga’s defence lawyer asks the judge to reduce the sentence because she is a young, single mother. This is an example of:
questions.answerNote: Personal circumstances may mitigate sentence.

questions.stem: Which group of factors constitute post-sentencing decisions?

options.A: Security classification, parole, level of violence used
options.B: Protective custody, sexual offenders registration, parole
options.C: Security classification, preventative and continued detention, age of the victim
options.D: Parole, criminal record of the victim, sexual offenders registration

questions.answerNote: Protective custody, sex offenders registration and parole are all post-sentencing (B); The other options include sentencing factors such as level of violence or victim's age/record.

questions.stem: Donald pleads guilty to a lesser charge in exchange for other charges being dropped. This is known as:
questions.answerNote: Charge negotiation is the NSW term for pleading guilty to a lesser charge in return for others being dropped (B). C 'Plea bargaining' is the informal equivalent, so two options are arguably correct.

questions.stem: When does an international treaty become enforceable in Australia?

options.A: When Australia becomes a signatory to the treaty
options.B: When the High Court of Australia ratifies the treaty
options.C: When the United Nations assents to the application of the treaty in Australia
options.D: When the government enacts legislation incorporating the treaty

questions.answerNote: Treaty provisions generally need implementing legislation to be enforceable domestically.

questions.stem: What is the role of the jury in a murder trial in NSW?

options.B: Determine the sentence of the accused
options.D: Determine innocence or guilt of the accused

questions.answerNote: The jury determines guilt; The judge rules on law and sentence.
